intro: Cost estimators judge risk, solve problems and manage numbers, skills that construction and engineering management value. The closest of the 25 careers below is Construction Managers, with an 86% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $114,990, which is 46% more than the $78,740 cost estimators earn.
why_it_works: Building an estimate means reading plans, pricing labor and materials and deciding where the risks are before a bid goes out. O*NET rates judgment at 3.62 out of 5 for this job and complex problem solving at 3.38. Construction management, industrial engineering and sales engineering use the same analysis. Almost every match needs no new degree. The gaps are site skills such as quality checks.
tips: Sales Engineers earn $124,900, which is 59% more, and are a 79% match.
Spend time on job sites; operations and quality knowledge is your main gap for construction management.
Purchasing Managers earn $148,080, or 88% more, and use your pricing and supplier knowledge.

faq.q: What jobs can former cost estimators do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Construction Managers (86%), Industrial Engineers (82%) and architectural and engineering managers (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Sales Engineers are also 79% matched and earn $124,900, which is 59% more than the $78,740 cost estimator median.

faq.q: Which careers for cost estimators pay more?
faq.a: 16 of the 25 matches pay more. Computer and Information Systems Managers earn $175,140 (122% more), architectural and engineering managers $171,270 (118% more) and Purchasing Managers $148,080 (88% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Engineering management usually needs a graduate degree.

faq.q: Do cost estimators need another degree?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than cost estimators already have, and only 1 usually needs a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 40% of workers in the closest match, so experience with bids counts most.

faq.q: What skills should cost estimators learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, quality control analysis, operation and control and troubleshooting. Coordination already rates 3.12 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so hands-on project knowledge is the main step toward construction management.
